chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man to whom death presented itself, so he freed his slave and made a bequest, and it was more than one-third. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The emancipation of the slave is enforced, and the deficit is taken from what remains.'
ai.seo_question: What is the priority of freeing a slave versus a bequest in Islamic inheritance law?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the procedural hierarchy in estate distribution, establishing that manumission (itq) is treated as a debt or immediate transfer that takes precedence over general bequests (wasiyyah). Consequently, if the bequest exceeds the permissible one-third limit, the shortfall is deducted from the bequeathed portion rather than reducing the value of the slave's freedom, reflecting the Shia juristic view that emancipation is a distinct, prioritized act of worship. This ensures the slave's status is secured before the remaining heirs or beneficiaries receive their shares.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Al A’ala Bin Razeyn, from Muhammad Bin Muslim,

(The narrator says) ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about a man, the death having presented itself to him, so he liberated his slave and bequeathed with a bequest. So it was more than the third. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Enforce the emancipation of the slave, and the deficit is regarding what remains’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Hakam from al-‘Ala’ ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has narrated the following:

“About the case of a man who when about to die sets free his slave and makes a will but the total is more than one-third of his legacy, abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘It is executed about the setting free of the slave and the deficit falls on the rest of the will.’”
